content.title: Blazers vs. Suns: How to watch NBA play-in game with playoff berth on the line
content.text: The Portland Trail Blazers face the Phoenix Suns in an NBA play-in game with a playoff berth on the line. Here’s how to watch, including time and streaming info. PORTLAND, Ore. — The Portland Trail Blazers are one win away from the playoffs — and one loss away from having to fight for their season. Portland travels to Phoenix to face the Suns (45-37) on Tuesday night in a high-stakes NBA play-in showdown. A win sends the Blazers into the playoffs. A loss means one more do-or-die game to keep its season alive. Portland has spent years rebuilding but enter this matchup after their strongest season in several years. What a win or loss means: Win: The Blazers advance to face the second-seeded San Antonio Spurs in the first round of the playoffs, starting SundayLoss: Portland returns home to face the winner of the Los Angeles Clippers vs. Golden State Warriors play-in game on FridayWin Friday's game: The Blazers advance to play the No. 1 seed Oklahoma City Thunder in the first round, starting Sunday This season, Portland (42-40) finished above .500 for the first time since 2020-21 and posted its highest win total since that season. The Blazers have been mired in mediocrity or worse for more than half a decade, but have shown gradual improvement over the past two seasons. Blazers season records (2019-20 to present): 2019-20: 35-392020-21: 42-302021-22: 27-552022-23: 33-492023-24: 21-612024-25: 36-462025-26: 42-40 Now in the play-in, Portland has two chances to win one game and secure a playoff berth. "It's going to be awesome for our guys to experience that and go through that," Blazers coach Tiago Splitter said. "A lot of guys are craving to be in that situation, especially the young guys. They're excited about it, and we all are, actually." How to watch Blazers vs. Suns The Portland Trail Blazers face the Phoenix Suns in an NBA play-in game on Tuesday with a playoff berth on the line. Time: 7 p.m. (PT)Location: PhoenixTV channel: Not available on traditional TVStreaming: Amazon Prime VideoRadio: Rip City Radio 620 AM (Portland) What channel is the Blazers vs. Suns game on tonight? The game will stream exclusively on Prime Video and will not air on a traditional TV channel. Top players to watch Two All-Stars. One elimination game. The spotlight will be on Deni Avdija and Devin Booker. Avdija has been the engine behind Portland's turnaround, earning his first All-Star nod while averaging 24.2 points, 6.9 rebounds and 6.7 assists. He's relentless attacking the rim and lives at the free-throw line, where he ranks among the league leaders in attempts. While his 3-point shooting dipped this season, his ability to score, create and draw contact makes him one of the toughest covers on the floor — and this will be his first taste of playoff pressure. Booker is no stranger to moments like this. The five-time All-Star continues to anchor Phoenix's offense, averaging 26.1 points and 6.0 assists. Though his 3-point shooting has slipped slightly the past two seasons, he remains one of the NBA's most dangerous scorers — and elevates his game in the postseason, where he's averaged 28 points across 47 career playoff games. Recent performance The Suns were 12 games above .500 at 39-27 on March 12 but stumbled down the stretch, losing 10 of their final 16 games. During that span, Phoenix ranked 17th in offense (115.2 points per 100 possessions) and 14th in defense (114.1). For the season, Phoenix ranks 17th in offense (114.2) and ninth in defense (112.9). The Blazers closed the season strong, winning 19 of their final 31 games. Over the same finishing 16-game stretch as Phoenix, Portland ranked 15th in offense (115.8) and first in defense (106.5). For the season, Portland ranks 21st in offense (113.1) and 12th in defense (113.5). Injury report Both teams could get key contributors back for Tuesday's play-in matchup. The Blazers have upgraded forward Jerami Grant to questionable for Tuesday's game. He's been out since late March with a right calf strain. If he plays Tuesday, he'll likely be on a 15- to 20-minute restriction. Grant ranks third on the Blazers in scoring at 18.6 points per game, 3-point attempts at 6.1 per game, and 3-point accuracy at 38.9%. Grayson Allen, who missed the last game of the season for the Suns with left hamstring soreness, is also listed as questionable.
